unit.title: Aspectual verbal periphrases
unit.subtitle: venir, andar, ir, llevar + gerund and result periphrases

grammar.title: The nuance a helper verb adds to the gerund
grammar.intro: Spanish loads huge amounts of aspect onto simple gerund periphrases. Llevo dos horas esperando tells you how long; vengo diciéndolo tells you it's been building up for a while; voy entendiendo tells you it's happening gradually; anda buscando trabajo tells you it's scattered and repeated. Choosing the right auxiliary is pure C1 finesse.

sections.heading: How long, and building up: llevar / venir + gerund
sections.body: Llevar + gerund measures the duration of an ongoing action up to now — it replaces ‘have been -ing for’. Venir + gerund stresses that the action has been accumulating from the past toward the present:
conj: I've been studying it for three years
How long have you been waiting?
Te lo vengo diciendo hace tiempo
I've been telling you for a while
The problem has been dragging on

ex.en: I've been waiting for the train for two hours.

ex.es: Te lo vengo diciendo desde hace meses.
ex.en: I've been telling you this for months.
ex.note: venir + gerund = accumulated from the past

sections.heading: Gradual vs. scattered: ir / andar + gerund
sections.body: Ir + gerund marks a gradual, step-by-step change — progress unfolding little by little. Andar + gerund marks a repeated or scattered activity, often with a mildly critical or dismissive tone:
conj: Start turning off the lights (one by one)
He's going around looking for a flat

ex.es: Poco a poco voy entendiendo el subjuntivo.
ex.en: Little by little I'm coming to understand the subjunctive.

ex.es: Últimamente anda buscando trabajo por todas partes.
ex.en: Lately he's been going around looking for work everywhere.

sections.heading: Accumulated result: tener / ir + participle, acabar + gerund
sections.body: Tener + participle and ir + participle express an accumulated result — and the participle agrees with the object (tengo escritas tres cartas). Acabar/terminar + gerund means ‘to end up doing’, and dar por + participle means ‘to consider something done’:
conj: A hundred tickets sold so far
He ended up accepting the offer
I take it for granted you'll come

ex.en: I've already got three letters written.

ex.es: Tras mucho dudar, acabó aceptando la oferta.
ex.en: After much hesitation, he ended up accepting the offer.
ex.note: acabar + gerund = to end up doing

takeaways: llevar + gerund = how long something has been going on: Llevo dos horas esperando.
venir + gerund = a process built up from the past; ir + gerund = gradual, step-by-step change.
andar + gerund = a repeated or scattered action, often with a critical tone.
tener/ir + participle = accumulated result (participle agrees); acabar + gerund = to end up doing; dar por + participle = to consider it done.

mistakes.why: In this durative sense llevar takes a gerund (esperando), not an infinitive.
With tener + participle the participle agrees with the object: cartas → escritas (fem. plural).
‘To end up doing’ is acabar + gerund (aceptando), never acabar a + infinitive.

exercises.prompt: ___ dos horas esperando el autobús y no llega.
exercises.prompt_en: I've been waiting for the bus for two hours and it isn't coming.
exercises.no: Duration up to now uses llevar + gerund: “Llevo dos horas esperando.”

exercises.prompt: Te lo ___ diciendo desde hace meses; deberías hacerme caso.
exercises.prompt_en: I've been telling you this for months; you should listen to me.
exercises.ok: ¡Exacto! Venir + gerundio = algo que se acumula desde el pasado.
exercises.no: For something built up over months, use venir + gerund: “te lo vengo diciendo”.
The participle agrees with cartas: “Tengo escritas tres cartas.”

exercises.prompt: Poco a poco ___ entendiendo el subjuntivo.
exercises.prompt_en: Little by little I'm coming to understand the subjunctive.
exercises.no: Gradual progress uses ir + gerund: “voy entendiendo”.

exercises.prompt: Match each periphrasis to the nuance it adds.

exercises.tts: Anda buscando piso por el centro.
accepted: anda buscando piso por el centro
exercises.translation: He's going around looking for a flat downtown.
exercises.no: It was: “Anda buscando piso por el centro.” (andar + gerund = scattered).

exercises.scenario: You ask a colleague how a friend's job offer turned out 💼

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.es: Oye, ¿al final qué hizo Ana con la oferta de trabajo?
lines.en: Hey, what did Ana finally do about the job offer?

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Acabar + gerundio = to end up doing.
exercises.no: ‘Ended up accepting it’ is acabar + gerund: “acabó aceptándola”.

exercises.say: Llevo media hora buscando las llaves.
exercises.en: I've been looking for the keys for half an hour.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound of “Llevo media hora buscando las llaves.”

vocab.en: to have been (doing) — accumulating from the past
